text: Three studies: (1) Using peptides from a synthetic combinatorial library, Bcr-Abl phosphorylated substrates more strongly than c-Abl, preferring peptides with positive charges. (2) c-Abl has three nuclear localization signals; its C terminus carries a leucine-rich nuclear export signal (NES) that complements NES-defective HIV Rev (RevΔ3NI), exports GST, is leptomycin B-sensitive, and is abolished by L1064A. NES-mutated c-Abl localizes exclusively to the nucleus; leptomycin B accumulates wild-type c-Abl nuclearly; c-Abl NES(-) persists in nuclei of fibroblasts replated on fibronectin. c-Abl shuttles continuously, modulated by cell adherence. (3) In BDF1 mice, small-intestinal apoptosis peaked at crypt position 4 (stem-cell region); colonic apoptosis was attenuated and distributed. bcl-2 occurred at colonic crypt bases but was absent in small-intestinal crypts, including positions 4–5.
